title: Method for full protein sequence mapping: LC-MS analysis
protocol: Perform microcapillary reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) separation.
Interface the RP-HPLC with an electrospray ionization source.
Cut a segment of fused silica glass capillary for use as an HPLC column.
Burn off a segment of polyimide coating from the capillary using a small flame.
Shape a bottleneck into the glass capillary using a laser puller.
Load reversed-phase packing material behind the bottleneck in the capillary.
Force slurry containing C-18 packing material into the capillary tube using helium gas at about 500 psi.
Pull an electrospray tip with inner diameter of 5-10 microns using a laser puller.
Load an aliquot of proteolytic digest onto the microcapillary HPLC column using a pressurized stainless steel bomb.
Connect a pre-column to the main capillary column using a Teflon sleeve for sample volumes greater than 5 μl.
Connect the microcapillary column to the HPLC solvent line.
Run a gradient of increasingly organic solvent across the microcapillary HPLC column during analysis.
Apply 8.0 kV from the mass spectrometer to a stainless steel union on the HPLC waste line.
Maintain a flow rate of approximately 50 nL/min from the electrospray tip of the column.
Use a typical HPLC gradient of 0-80% organic solvent over a period of about 2 hours for highly complex peptide mixtures.
Ensure a low flow rate and shallow gradient to minimize the number of peptides being analyzed simultaneously by the mass spectrometer.
Use a Finnigan LTQ-FTMS instrument for full protein sequence mapping experiments.
Combine linear ion trap and Fourier Transform ion cyclotron resonance mass analysis technologies.
Achieve sub-femtomole limit of detection.
Increase dynamic range by approximately 50-fold.
Obtain high mass resolution of 100,000 at m/z 400.
Determine accurate mass with external calibration to within 1-3 ppm.
Increase scan speed to 5 scans per second.
Analyze complex mixtures such as binding partner pull-downs for useful information.
Sift through MS/MS data quickly from single protein pull-downs.
Assign sequence and post-translational modification information to spectra.
Set up software for non-redundant mass spectra acquisition.
Acquire one full range MS scan (300-2000 m/z).
Choose the top ten most abundant ions above a signal threshold for MS/MS analysis.
Fragment chosen peptide ions by collision with helium atoms to produce fragment ions.
Place the ten most abundant peptide ions on a dynamic exclusion list.
Repeat acquisition cycle, taking another full MS scan.
Select next ten most abundant ions not previously excluded for MS/MS analysis.
Continue cycles of MS and MS/MS scans throughout data acquisition.
